statement: Let nonX(s) be the byte sequence obtained from s by deleting every occurrence of 'X'. For a byte sequence s and an index j with 0 <= j < len(nonX(s)), let pos(s,j) be the index in s of the j-th byte of nonX(s), counted from 0. The function returns a result r and r = true if and only if: (1) nonX(start) = nonX(result), and (2) for every j with 0 <= j < len(nonX(start)), if nonX(start)[j] = 'L' then pos(start,j) >= pos(result,j), and if nonX(start)[j] = 'R' then pos(start,j) <= pos(result,j).
preconditions: len(start) = len(result); 1 <= len(start) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(start), start[i] and result[i] are one of the bytes 'L', 'R', 'X' (ASCII 76, 82, 88).

statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail: there is no panic, out-of-bounds access, arithmetic overflow, or other runtime failure.
preconditions: len(start) = len(result); 1 <= len(start) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(start), start[i] and result[i] are one of the bytes 'L', 'R', 'X' (ASCII 76, 82, 88).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if r = true then the sequence of non-'X' bytes of start equals the sequence of non-'X' bytes of result.
preconditions: len(start) = len(result); 1 <= len(start) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(start), start[i] and result[i] are one of the bytes 'L', 'R', 'X' (ASCII 76, 82, 88).

statement: Whenever the function returns r = true, for every j with 0 <= j < number of 'L' bytes in start, the index in start of the j-th 'L' byte is greater than or equal to the index in result of the j-th 'L' byte. Here the j-th 'L' is counted from 0 among the 'L' bytes only, and the j-th 'L' of result is defined because r = true implies equal numbers of 'L' bytes.
preconditions: len(start) = len(result); 1 <= len(start) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(start), start[i] and result[i] are one of the bytes 'L', 'R', 'X' (ASCII 76, 82, 88).

statement: Let start' be the byte array of length len(start)+1 with start'[0] = 'X' and start'[i+1] = start[i] for every 0 <= i < len(start), and define result' analogously from result. Then the Boolean returned by the function on (start',result') equals the Boolean returned on (start,result).
preconditions: len(start) = len(result); 1 <= len(start) < 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(start), start[i] and result[i] are one of the bytes 'L', 'R', 'X' (ASCII 76, 82, 88).
